papers.title: Cortical layer 6b mediates state-dependent changes in brain activity and effects of orexin on waking and sleep.
papers.summary: The study silenced a subset of cortical layer 6b neurons in mice and found reduced EEG power, particularly in NREM sleep, and a slowing of theta frequency during wake and REM sleep. The response to orexin A was altered, suggesting L6b neurons regulate state-dependent brain oscillations.

papers.title: An Evidence-Aware Framework for EEG Microstate Analysis: Improved Sensitivity to Alzheimer's Disease and Ageing
papers.summary: The paper introduces a template evidence trajectory framework for EEG microstate analysis that retains evidence strength at each GFP peak, unlike traditional hard-label approaches. Across 32 dataset-model cases, trajectory-derived duration effects exceeded hard-label effects in all cases, and null-state Lempel-Ziv complexity improved over traditional complexity, providing more sensitive readouts of topographic state dynamics.

papers.title: Repetitive circadian disruption contributes to pain hypersensitivity and alters the transcriptional rhythms in spinal cord in male mice with neuropathic pain.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of three weeks of chronic jet lag (repetitive circadian disruption) on pain sensitivity and spinal cord transcriptional rhythms in male mice with spared nerve injury (SNI). Results showed that circadian disruption reduced mechanical thresholds and altered rhythmic transcripts, with SNI mice exhibiting fewer rhythmic transcripts under jet lag, indicating that circadian disruption exacerbates pain and disrupts spinal transcriptomic rhythms.

papers.title: Tau-associated neuronal loss in the intermediate nucleus of the human hypothalamus, a putative VLPO analog, in progressive supranuclear palsy and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: This postmortem study examined neuronal loss and tau pathology in the intermediate nucleus (IntN) of the hypothalamus in progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). They found profound IntN degeneration in PSP (84% neuron reduction) and progressive loss of galanin-positive neurons in higher AD stages, suggesting disease-specific vulnerability consistent with sleep phenotype differences.

papers.title: Specification dependence of EEG theta/alpha ratio associations with cognitive impairment: a multiverse analysis
papers.summary: This multiverse analysis examined the robustness of EEG theta/alpha ratio associations with cognitive impairment across 1,280 analytic specifications in Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, and frontotemporal dementia datasets. Findings varied across specifications, but consistent associations emerged under specific analytic choices (e.g., ICA with absolute power), indicating the marker is promising but specification-dependent.

papers.title: Sleep, circadian rhythms, chronobiology, and neural synchrony: Integrative mechanisms in brain function, health, and disease.
papers.summary: This review integrates mechanisms of sleep, circadian rhythms, chronobiology, and neural synchrony, detailing how the suprachiasmatic nucleus, clock gene feedback loops, and thalamocortical circuits coordinate brain function. It also highlights therapeutic avenues like chronotherapy and AI-based sleep analysis, emphasizing the intersection of chronobiology and neuroscience.

papers.title: Xylazine Reshapes the Sleep and Respiratory Consequences of Chronic Fentanyl Exposure in a Sex-Dependent Manner
papers.summary: This preprint study compared chronic fentanyl and xylazine exposure, alone and combined, in male and female mice. Combined exposure produced distinct sex-dependent alterations in sleep architecture and exacerbated respiratory depression, particularly in males, while increasing peripheral FGF21 levels.

papers.title: Suppression of corticospinal excitability by sleep spindles without increase in GABAergic inhibition
papers.summary: This study used real-time EEG-triggered transcranial magnetic stimulation to test whether sleep spindle-related suppression of corticospinal excitability is mediated by GABA-Aergic inhibition. They found that spindles suppress corticospinal excitability without altering short-interval intracortical inhibition, suggesting distinct contributions of vigilance states and slow oscillations.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals cell-type-specific circadian rhythms and their disruption by acute misalignment in mouse aorta
papers.summary: This study performed single-cell RNA sequencing of mouse aorta under aligned and acutely misaligned light-dark cycles, identifying cell-type-specific circadian rhythms and their disruption by misalignment. They found hundreds of cycling genes in vascular smooth muscle cells and fibroblasts, with sex differences and molecular evidence of proteostatic stress after misalignment.

papers.title: Are infraslow oscillations the missing link between sleep and Alzheimer's?
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: The study analyzed NREM sleep EEG in Alzheimer's disease (AD) participants and controls, finding reduced infraslow oscillation (ISO) peak amplitude in AD with preserved frequency and bandwidth. ISO amplitude trended with Aβ42/40, and bandwidth was associated with NfL, suggesting ISO may link sleep and AD pathology.

papers.title: Mapping and modulating brain dynamics in aging and neurodegeneration with electroencephalography and integrated neurotechnologies in primates.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes EEG methodologies in non-human primates (NHPs), highlighting their value as a translational platform for studying aging and neurodegeneration. It summarizes EEG signatures in normal aging and disease models, and discusses integration with other modalities and neuromodulation techniques to test causality and translate findings to humans.

papers.title: Tracing melanin-concentrating hormone function: decades of memory research and emerging links to Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: This mini-review summarizes studies on melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH) in memory, noting its complex role in promoting consolidation, inducing forgetting during REM sleep, or negatively regulating memory formation. It also discusses emerging links to Alzheimer's disease, including therapeutic potential and effects on sleep architecture.

papers.title: Sleep timing regulates mood: A multilevel-EEG study of daily life.
papers.summary: This 7-day observational study of 258 healthy adults used EEG headbands and multilevel modeling to show that later sleep onset predicts lower next-day positive affect, while higher evening positive affect predicts later sleep onset, forming a bidirectional feedback loop. The association was moderated by personality traits such as activity, extraversion, conscientiousness, neuroticism, and alexithymia.

papers.title: Insomnia phenotypes and neurocognitive biomarkers.
papers.summary: This review develops a phenotype-informed framework for insomnia, distinguishing clinical presentations from mechanistic dimensions and biomarker domains. It reviews neurocognitive biomarkers, electrophysiological and sleep microstructure markers, and multimodal approaches, concluding that no single biomarker is sufficient and that integrative phenotyping can guide individualized treatment.

papers.title: Sleep homeostasis in OSA: a complementary neurophysiological outcome measure.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
papers.summary: This article discusses sleep homeostasis in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) as a potential complementary neurophysiological outcome measure, but the abstract was not provided. The journal is the Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine.

papers.title: Neurobiology of sleep apnea and cognitive impairment.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that obstructive sleep apnea impairs cognition through intermittent hypoxia, sleep fragmentation, neuroinflammation, and structural brain changes, and highlights that domain-sensitive cognitive assessment and effective PAP therapy (especially REM coverage) are important for outcomes.

papers.title: Hippocampal CA1 neurons are crucial for sleep-associated memory formation in humans: The role of theta power during NREM sleep
papers.summary: This study on patients with transient global amnesia (TGA) found that hippocampal CA1 lesions impair sleep-dependent memory consolidation and reduce NREM theta power, which predicted consolidation improvements. Other NREM markers like spindles were unaffected, suggesting theta power reflects hippocampal integrity.

papers.title: Environmental Enrichment Enhances Visual Function in Adult Amblyopia: Association With miR-132/HDAC3 Regulation.
papers.summary: In an adult amblyopic mouse model, environmental enrichment improved visual function (increased flash visual evoked potential amplitude) and upregulated miR-132 while downregulating HDAC3 in the primary visual cortex; in vitro, miR-132 directly targeted HDAC3 and promoted structural remodeling of cortical neurons.

papers.title: Reactivating a Relaxation Exercise During Sleep to Influence Cortical Hyperarousal in Individuals With Frequent Nightmares.
papers.summary: In individuals with frequent nightmares, reactivating a relaxation-associated odor cue during sleep did not reduce cortical hyperarousal (beta/gamma power) or nightmare symptoms, but unexpectedly reduced spindle count and density. Spindle count correlated positively with subjective wake-after-sleep-onset.

papers.title: EEG Reactivity and Etiology as Prognostic Modifiers in Alpha and Theta Coma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of alpha/theta coma found that overall mortality was 74% and severe disability or death occurred in 83.7%, but EEG reactivity was associated with lower mortality (OR 5.67 for nonreactive) and higher odds of favorable outcome (OR 8.68 for reactive), while etiology (toxic/metabolic vs hypoxic-ischemic) further modulated prognosis.

papers.title: Muscle-Specific Upregulation of Timeless Mediates Exercise-Induced Amelioration of Age-Related Circadian Rhythm Disruption and Cardiac Dysfunction in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Using Drosophila, this study showed that muscle-specific knockdown of Timeless accelerates age-related circadian and cardiac dysfunction, while overexpression delays it. A 4-week endurance exercise regimen counteracted the effects of knockdown and further improved outcomes in aged flies, suggesting exercise acts through Timeless upregulation.

papers.title: Transient Sleep Deprivation Induces Persistent Auditory Neuropathy via ROS-Initiated Neuroinflammation and BK Channel Suppression.
papers.summary: This study establishes a dose-dependent association between sleep disturbance severity and hearing loss in patients, and uses a mouse model to show that acute sleep deprivation causes persistent high-frequency hearing loss via cochlear synaptopathy. The mechanism involves transient oxidative stress initiating chronic neuroinflammation that suppresses BK channels, and antioxidant or BK channel opener treatment prevents the deficits.

papers.title: Closed-loop auditory stimulation in phase with slow waves during sleep enhances cerebrospinal fluid flow in humans.
papers.summary: This study developed closed-loop auditory stimulation synchronized with slow-wave peaks during sleep and used simultaneous MRI to show that it enhances cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow waves in healthy adults. The effect was phase-dependent and accompanied by widespread hemodynamic waves, demonstrating a causal link between neural slow waves and CSF flow.

papers.title: Smartphone-based digital phenotyping of sighted non-24-h sleep-wake disorder: A 258-d continuous circadian monitoring study.
papers.summary: This study presents a 258-day smartphone-based digital phenotyping method for monitoring circadian rhythms in a sighted individual with Non-24-h sleep-wake disorder. The smartphone-derived circadian period (25.16 h) closely matched actigraphy (25.11 h), demonstrating its utility as a low-burden alternative for long-term circadian monitoring.

papers.title: Dose-response meta-analysis of dual orexin receptor antagonists on sleep parameters and implications for orexin-mediated arousal.
papers.summary: This dose-response meta-analysis of 21 randomized controlled trials of dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs) for insomnia found dose-related improvements in sleep continuity that plateau within approved dose ranges. Effects were larger initially and slightly attenuated with repeated use, while sleep architecture was largely preserved, arguing against supratherapeutic dosing.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm Disruption in Alzheimer's Disease: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Implications, and Therapeutic Approaches.
papers.summary: This review examines the interplay between circadian rhythm disruption and Alzheimer's disease, highlighting that circadian gene dysregulation exacerbates tau and amyloid pathology, and discusses therapeutic approaches like light therapy and melatonin. It emphasizes the need for integrated and personalized circadian-based therapies.

papers.title: Prognostic assessment of comatose patients after cardiac arrest: construction of a simplified monitoring EEG risk score across different time windows.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study developed a Simplified EEG Risk Score (SERS) for prognostic assessment in 251 comatose patients after cardiac arrest. SERS incorporated EEG features such as background amplitude, dominant frequency, continuity, reactivity, and sleep elements, achieving high AUCs (0.881-0.912) across time windows and outperforming individual EEG features and clinical predictors.

papers.title: A Rapid Workflow For Modeling Sleep Deprivation-Induced Recognition Memory Deficits In Mice Using Novel Object Recognition and Hippocampal Biomarkers.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a rapid workflow for modeling sleep deprivation-induced recognition memory deficits in mice using a 5-hour gentle-handling sleep deprivation after novel object recognition training. The workflow links behavioral outcomes to hippocampal inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, emphasizing standardization and reproducibility.

papers.title: A Dual Soft Attention Network for Automatic Sleep Staging via Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Signals.
papers.summary: This paper proposes SleepECGNet, a dual soft attention network for automatic sleep staging using single-lead ECG signals. The model, evaluated on HMC, MGH, and SHHS1 datasets, improved classification with expanded input timeframes and showed transferability to sleep apnea recognition using the Apnea-ECG corpus.

papers.title: Developmental myelination deficits and impaired fine motor function in a mouse model of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: This study used a mouse model of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (POSA) to show that fine motor deficits are associated with developmental myelination deficits, reduced oligodendrocyte progenitor cells, and altered oligodendrocyte transcriptome, without changes in gross motor function.

papers.title: Whole-brain mapping of choline acetyltransferase neurons expression in tree shrew compared with mice.
papers.summary: This study systematically mapped the whole-brain distribution and morphology of choline acetyltransferase-immunoreactive (ChAT-ir) neurons in the tree shrew and compared them with those in mice, revealing key interspecies differences such as absence of cortical ChAT-ir neurons in the tree shrew and higher density in specific subcortical nuclei. The findings provide a structural framework for studying cholinergic roles in neural functions.

papers.title: An Intraoperative EEG Biomarker for Postoperative Delirium Predicting Based on Interpretable Deep Learning Framework.
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable deep learning framework using intraoperative EEG to predict postoperative delirium with high accuracy, identifying a frontal 2-12 Hz oscillation biomarker. The biomarker was validated externally, supporting its use for early warning and individualized care.

papers.title: Polysomnographic characteristics of excessive daytime sleepiness in postmenopausal women with obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study in postmenopausal women with obstructive sleep apnea found that excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) was independently associated with higher respiratory disturbance index (total, supine, REM, NREM) and lower oxygen saturation. A four-variable model (RDI, REM RDI, mean and minimum oxygen saturation) had moderate discriminative ability (AUROC 0.693).

papers.title: Aquaporin-4 mis-localization decreases glymphatic clearance of α-synuclein in an alpha-syntrophin knock out mouse model and promotes α-synuclein pathology and aggregate propagation.
papers.summary: This study demonstrated that mis-localization of aquaporin-4, as seen in alpha-syntrophin knockout mice, impairs glymphatic clearance of α-synuclein and promotes α-synuclein aggregate propagation. Human post-mortem cortex also showed that α-synuclein pathology is associated with aquaporin-4 mis-localization, linking glymphatic dysfunction to synucleinopathy progression.

papers.title: Routine Blood Indicators Combined With Sleep Questionnaires for the Identification of Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson's Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study With a Leakage-Free Nested Modeling Framework.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 347 Parkinson's disease patients developed a leakage-free nested modeling framework combining routine blood indicators and sleep questionnaires to identify cognitive impairment, achieving a test-set AUC of 0.943 in the full logistic regression model, which significantly outperformed a clinical baseline model.

papers.title: REM sleep behavior disorder and synucleinopathies.
papers.summary: This review discusses REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) as a key early indicator for synucleinopathies, covering biomarkers, neuroimaging, and fluid-based markers for risk stratification. It also highlights RBD as a window for testing neuroprotective therapies and reviews current management approaches including pharmacological and neuromodulation strategies.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics profiling of insomnia-related molecular features reveals microbiome, immune, and therapy-relevant heterogeneity in colorectal cancer.
papers.summary: This study integrated multi-omics data from 3,026 colorectal cancer patients to identify two insomnia-related molecular subtypes (IS1/IS2) with distinct survival, immune infiltration, and intratumoral microbiome profiles. An insomnia score (ISscore) was developed and validated, showing association with immunotherapy response indicators and stratifying survival risk.

papers.title: Sleep and Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction.
papers.summary: This review discusses the prevalence and impact of sleep disorders on disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs), including functional dyspepsia and irritable bowel syndrome. It covers mechanisms linking sleep disruption to brain-gut axis dysfunction and provides practical tips for evaluating and treating patients with both conditions.

papers.title: From a Pinched Nerve to a Fatal Prognosis: Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease Masquerading as Cervical Myelopathy.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 53-year-old man with sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease initially presenting with symptoms mimicking cervical myelopathy, leading to diagnostic delay and surgical intervention. Diagnosis was confirmed by positive RT-QuIC and elevated CSF tau and 14-3-3 proteins, and the patient declined to death.

papers.title: Association between circadian rhythm sleep disorders and dry eye disease: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study using real-world clinical data from 48,356 patients found that circadian rhythm sleep disorders were associated with a significantly increased risk of dry eye disease over 1, 3, and 5 years after propensity score matching. The adjusted hazard ratios ranged from 2.31 at 1 year to 2.04 at 5 years.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
